In this case, we have to use the identity  $1+{cot}^{2}⁡x={csc}^{2}⁡x.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}({sin}^{3}⁡x+{cot}^{2}⁡x{sin}^{3}⁡x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sin}^{3}⁡x(1+{cot}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sin}^{3}⁡x{csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}{sin}^{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,{|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /3} \\  & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
